description: A rectilinear, low‐relief embankment or causeway running almost due north–south. In the hillshade it appears as a subtle raised line ~4 m wide and >2 km long, unnaturally straight compared to the surrounding microtopography. Its linearity and consistent cross‐section suggest deliberate earth‐moving for transport or raised walkway.

A crossing east–west drainage ditch or canal dissecting the N–S embankment at roughly right angles. Visible as a shallow, linear depression ~2 m wide and ~800 m long. In the NIR, the feature aligns with a narrow band of slightly elevated moisture signature (‘dark earth’) and vegetation stress.

A curvilinear channel following an S‐shape near the southern third of the tile. ~50 m across at its widest, it appears as a gently cut embankment (or ponded area) in the DTM and shows a brighter tone in hillshade—consistent with moisture‐retaining earthen works, perhaps for fish‐ponds or sediment traps.
